Eye Disorders

Eye disorders — conjunctivitis, cataract, glaucoma, retinal detachment — assessment and nursing care.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Describe common eye disorders
  • Explain nursing care for eye patients
  • State post-operative eye care instructions

In simple terms

Eye disorders affect vision and eye health — common problems include conjunctivitis, cataract, glaucoma, retinal detachment and eye injuries. Nurses assess vision, administer eye medications and teach eye care.

Common eye disorders

Disorder Cause/Features Key signs
Conjunctivitis Conjunctiva inflammation (viral/bacterial/allergic) Red eye, discharge, itching, gritty sensation
Cataract Lens clouding (age-related) Blurred vision, glare sensitivity, faded colours
Glaucoma Increased intraocular pressure Gradual vision loss, halos around lights, eye pain (acute)
Retinal detachment Retina separates from underlying tissue Floaters, flashes, curtain-like vision loss
Conjunctivitis (pink eye) Conjunctiva inflammation Red eye, discharge, itching, gritty sensation

Nursing care

  • Eye drops — wash hands, tilt head back, pull lower lid down, instill drop into conjunctival sac, press punctum 1 minute.
  • Eye ointment — instill into lower conjunctival sac from inner to outer canthus.
  • Eye patch — apply as ordered; do not patch both eyes unless ordered.
  • Post-operative care (cataract surgery) — no rubbing, no bending over, no heavy lifting, shield at night, report sudden vision loss.

Nursing care points

  • Visual acuity — assess with Snellen chart; document changes.
  • Eye hygiene — clean crusts/discharge with warm water and cotton wool; wipe from inner to outer canthus.
  • Medication administration — eye drops before ointment; wait 5 minutes between different drops.
  • Patient teaching — eye drop technique, hand hygiene, avoid rubbing eyes, report sudden vision changes.

🔴 Retinal detachment = emergency

Retinal detachment is an ophthalmic emergency. Sudden floaters, flashes of light, or curtain-like vision loss — report immediately. Delayed treatment can cause permanent vision loss.

Where the nurse uses this

  • Eye drop administration — wash hands, check correct eye/drug, instill into conjunctival sac (not directly on cornea), press punctum 1 minute, wait 5 minutes between different drops.
  • Visual acuity assessment — use Snellen chart; document changes; report sudden vision loss.
  • Post-operative care (cataract surgery) — no rubbing, no bending over, no heavy lifting, wear eye shield at night, avoid swimming.
  • Patient teaching — eye drop technique, hand hygiene, avoid rubbing eyes, report sudden vision changes or severe eye pain.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Conjunctivitis = conjunctiva inflammation; red eye, discharge, itching, gritty sensation.
  2. Cataract = lens clouding (age-related); blurred vision, glare sensitivity, faded colours.
  3. Glaucoma = increased intraocular pressure; gradual vision loss, halos around lights, eye pain (acute).
  4. Retinal detachment = retina separates from underlying tissue; floaters, flashes, curtain-like vision loss.
  5. Eye drops: instill into conjunctival sac, press punctum 1 minute, wait 5 minutes between different drops.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Cataract surgery: no rubbing, no bending over, no heavy lifting, wear eye shield at night.
  2. Retinal detachment = emergency; sudden floaters, flashes, curtain-like vision loss — report immediately.
  3. Glaucoma: lifelong medication adherence; regular eye pressure monitoring.
  4. Conjunctivitis: hand hygiene, avoid sharing towels/pillows, dispose of tissues properly.

📌 Memory trick

Eye drops: T.I.P.S. — Tilt head back, Pull lower lid down, Instill into conjunctival sac, press punctum/Stop blinking for 1 minute.

60-second revision

  • Eye disorders: conjunctivitis, cataract, glaucoma, retinal detachment.
  • Cataract = lens clouding; glaucoma = increased intraocular pressure.
  • Retinal detachment = emergency; floaters, flashes, curtain-like vision loss.
  • Eye drops: instill into conjunctival sac, press punctum 1 minute.
  • Cataract surgery: no rubbing, no bending over, no heavy lifting.

Test yourself

Cataract is:

Answer: A. Cataract = clouding of the eye lens; causes blurred vision, glare sensitivity, faded colours.

Glaucoma is characterized by:

Answer: B. Glaucoma = increased intraocular pressure; can cause gradual vision loss and blindness if untreated.

Retinal detachment signs include:

Answer: B. Retinal detachment = floaters, flashes of light, curtain-like vision loss; ophthalmic emergency.

Eye drops should be instilled into:

Answer: B. Eye drops should be instilled into the conjunctival sac (lower lid pocket), not directly on the cornea.

After cataract surgery, patient should:

Answer: B. After cataract surgery: no rubbing, no bending over, no heavy lifting, wear eye shield at night.
